subject.title: feat(backup): add exclude patterns, --smart-exclude, and protected path guards [ai]

question: Should OpenClaw core land native backup exclude support with this PR's full `.backupignore`/smart-default/protected-path contract, or require a narrower opt-in design before merge?
rationale: This PR adds public CLI flags and config-like backup behavior that affects security, restore completeness, and large-backup availability, so automation should not choose the final backup policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require safer native exclude contract
options.body: Keep the PR open and require explicit `.backupignore` opt-in, per-asset-root filtering, ordered rule preservation, bounded integrity checking, docs, and real backup proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to curated built-in skips
options.body: Ask for a replacement or major rewrite that only adds maintainer-defined safe omissions for large backups and defers arbitrary user patterns.

options.title: Defer native excludes
options.body: Close or pause this PR and keep core backup policy limited to current coarse scopes while external backup tools cover custom filtering.

recommendation.title: Require safer native exclude contract
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open and require explicit `.backupignore` opt-in, per-asset-root filtering, ordered rule preservation, bounded integrity checking, docs, and real backup proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: gumadeiras has the strongest verified history on backup path extraction and verify hardening, which are central to the restore-safety decision.
